packageRules.description: Major updates: one PR per package. A major usually breaks the API surface, so it is the update most likely to break CI — isolating each one keeps that break cheap to diagnose and fix. Automerge stays on: the gate is CI, which is maintained to a standard where green means shippable without human testing. groupName: null overrides any inherited monorepo group from config:recommended.

Rust compiler: its own PR, for the same reason majors get one. A compiler bump lands new default-on clippy lints across the whole crate at once (see rust-toolchain.toml), which under `-D warnings` breaks CI on code that never changed — isolating it keeps that break cheap to fix. Automerge stays on: CI is the gate. No matchDepNames filter: this manager only reads rust-toolchain.toml, so every dep it produces is the compiler, and a filter that stopped matching would silently demote the bump into another rule. Last rule wins — keep this LAST.
